walkthroughs.body_html:
Introduction to Business Management — a core area of Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Introduction to Business Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Introduction to Business Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
Just-in-time means finishing work right before the deadline.
Holding minimal stock and receiving inputs only when needed for production — reducing storage costs but increasing vulnerability to supply disruption.
Just-in-time means delivering products to customers exactly on time.
Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
Porter's Five Forces are five business strategies a firm should choose between.

Competitive rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of suppliers, bargaining power of buyers — together determining industry attractiveness and potential profitability.

mcqs.q: What three Ps are added to make the extended marketing mix (7Ps)?
options: Porter's Five Forces are five physical security measures for a factory.
The 7Ps are just the 4Ps repeated with different words.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
People (staff/service quality), Process (how the service is delivered), and Physical Evidence (tangible cues — uniforms, packaging, branding) — added to make the 4Ps relevant to services marketing.
